name: Riga International Biennial of Contemporary Art (RIBOCA)
funding: Private. Founded by Agniya Mirgorodskaya, daughter of Russian fishing businessman Gennady Mirgorodsky. The organisers said funding moved to a US charity, Just A Moment, after 2022.
watch: Curator Žanete Liekīte campaigned against it; four artists withdrew on 30 June 2023. The organisers suspended the third edition in July 2023.
why_flagged: Private. Founded by Agniya Mirgorodskaya, daughter of Russian fishing businessman Gennady Mirgorodsky. The organisers said funding moved to a US charity, Just A Moment, after 2022. No state funder confirmed.
records_note: Its website address is now a parked for-sale page, so its reports, accounts, funders and board are unchecked.

name: Rijksmuseum
watch: Ended Saudi Aramco 2017; XR targets ING.
why_flagged: Ended Saudi Aramco 2017; XR targets ING.
records_note: It posts Dutch annual reports for 2021 to 2025 with financials, names main partners ING, KPN and Vriendenloterij, and has pages for its boards.

name: Royal Ballet and Opera
records_note: It posts annual reviews and reports from 2005/06 to 2024/25 with accounts, names philanthropists and sponsors by tier (updated April 2025), and lists its trustees.

name: Royal Philharmonic Orchestra
watch: Prince Andrew was the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra's patron, and the orchestra thanked him for his support "over the past 15 years". In November 2019 its board decided to "part company with its patron, with immediate effect".
why_flagged: Corporate partners include Northern Trust, dunhill and Chapel Down; trusts include the Linbury Trust, Stavros Niarchos Foundation and D'Oyly Carte. Arts Council England's logo is on its supporter page.
records_note: Accounts for 2023 to 2025 are at Companies House; the site names supporters and 16 directors and trustees but posts no annual report.

name: Ruarts Foundation
watch: Foundation founded 2003; opened its own building 2021; runs street-art grants. Sardarov is not on EU, UK or US sanctions lists.
why_flagged: Foundation founded 2003; opened its own building 2021; runs street-art grants. Sardarov is not on EU, UK or US sanctions lists.
records_note: The foundation posts no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; its About page names founder Marianna Sardarova and art director Catherine Borissoff.

name: Russian Pavilion at the Venice Biennale
watch: Artists Savchenkov and Sukhareva and curator Malašauskas quit in Feb 2022 and the pavilion stayed shut; lent to Bolivia in 2024 and to a Thomas Heatherwick project in 2025 (protested by the Ukrainian pavilion's co-curator); 2026 return curated by Anastasia Karneeva prompted the European Commission to threaten the Biennale's EU funding (Mar 2026).
why_flagged: Artists Savchenkov and Sukhareva and curator Malašauskas quit in Feb 2022 and the pavilion stayed shut; lent to Bolivia in 2024 and to a Thomas Heatherwick project in 2025 (protested by the Ukrainian pavilion's co-curator); 2026 return curated by Anastasia Karneeva prompted the European Commission to threaten the Biennale's EU funding (Mar 2026).
records_note: The Russian Pavilion has no own site, reports, accounts, funder list or board; its commissioner is named in press but its funding is unpublished.

name: Ruya Foundation
watch: KAR Group, Kurdistan's largest private oil firm (Khurmala field, refineries), is on its sponsor list; the page dates from about 2015-18.

name: S.M.A.K.
funding: City of Ghent and Flanders. Current partners include the National Lottery, Belfius, Jan De Nul, Interparking, Christie's, Hiscox and Duvel. ENGIE has supported art workshops since 2012.
watch: Municipal contemporary museum of Ghent founded by Jan Hoet.
why_flagged: City of Ghent and Flanders. Current partners include the National Lottery, Belfius, Jan De Nul, Interparking, Christie's, Hiscox and Duvel. ENGIE has supported art workshops since 2012.

name: Séries Mania
watch: Caroline Lang held roles at Séries Mania, the Lille TV-series festival. La Voix du Nord first reported that she had to give them up after the US Justice Department released Epstein's emails.
why_flagged: Crédit Mutuel Nord Europe has been Grand Partenaire since the festival came to Lille in 2018, renewed in March 2026. No full funder list found.
records_note: The festival's site posts no annual report, accounts or board; partners appear only as logos in the footer, and the team page names directors.

name: School of Visual Arts
watch: Ross chaired SVA's MFA Art Practice department from 2009. In October 2009 Epstein proposed a "statutory" exhibition of "girls and boys ages 14 - 25", and Ross replied, "You are incredible."
why_flagged: Private art school in Manhattan. The Rhodes family owned it until 1 September 2025; the nonprofit SVA Alumni Society owns it now. No sponsor list found.
records_note: sva.edu posts no annual report, financial statements or donor list but names its 10-person board of trustees; no filings under the school's own name.

name: Science Museum
watch: Adani Green since 2024; BP ended only in August 2026.
why_flagged: Adani Green since 2024; BP ended only in August 2026.
records_note: Science Museum Group, its parent, posts annual reports and accounts for 2016 to 2024, names sponsors in the 2023-24 report, and lists trustees in them.

name: Seattle Art Museum
funding: Expenses $44.4M (FY2025); trustees, members, corporate partners, tech fortunes.
